concept.title: The agent hierarchy
concept.shortdesc: The Agents page shows the workspace's agents as a hierarchy of cards: who leads, which group each specialist is in, and who reports to whom. It is a picture of how the work is divided; no agent starts another, and each run is a run of one agent.

ul.li: The top card is the lead: an agent in no group that reports to no one. Below the top cards, a line totals everything on the page.
One column per group, each with a coloured marker and a summary line that totals the group's numbers. A group's colour comes from its name, so it is the same for everyone and on every visit.

Inside a column, the group's lead comes first and the agents that report to it are indented beneath it, joined by a guide line in the group's colour; nesting can go deeper. An agent with no group of its own sits in the group of the agent it reports to.

conbody.p: Each card has a coloured top border and a chip for its group, and shows its live numbers over the last 7 days: open runs (queued, running or waiting for approval), done runs, their cost, and the proposals of its runs waiting to approve. The numbers refresh while the page is open.

ul.li: Click a card to open the Runs page filtered to that agent: its runs, and the proposals waiting from them. The chip at the top of the Runs page clears the filter.
Mission and tools opens the agent's description, provider and model, write mode and allowed tools on the card.
▶ Launch starts a run; Edit agent opens the editor.

section.title: Arranging the hierarchy
section.p: A workspace admin clicks Edit (top right) to arrange the cards. Each card then shows:

ul.li: Reports to — the agent it sits under, or No one to put it at the top. An agent cannot report to itself or to an agent below it.
Group — type a group's name, pick an existing one, or clear it so the agent takes the group of the agent it reports to.
↑ ↓ — move it among the agents beside it.

section.p: Each change is saved at once, to the agent's definition file (reports_to, group and sort_order in its frontmatter). Click Done to leave Edit mode. The default agents arrive already arranged: the Chief of Staff on top, with Requirements, Verification and Engineering groups beneath it.
On a phone the groups stack in one column; tap a group's header to fold it.
Crews, the graphs of agents the Crew page used to build, have been removed; the hierarchy is how agents are arranged now.
